To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) action MACH is capable, with the same computational complexity as a traditional MACH filter, of synthesizing a single template for each human action class from a collection of training examples, (ii) the action MACH filter is able to generalize to unseen examples of the same action class, (iii) action MACH performs well in comparison with state of the art approaches, (iv) action MACH can be used in a variety of applications, including action recognition in feature films and
we propose a template based method that can be used for recognizing human actions, and the method is based on a spatio temporal maximum average correlation height filter for vector valued data.

1) action MACH, a spatiotemporeal maximum average correlation height filter, is an effective method for recognizing human action in video; 2) action MACH is capable to capture intra class variability by generating a single template for each action class; 3) action MACH outperforms state of the art methods in the recognition of human action in video.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How can we generate a single template from a set of examples?
developing a template based approach for action recognition.
the development of a template based approach for recognizing actions in video sequences.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the action MACH filter outperforms all the methods tested in this work, including state of the art methods such as HMAX, SVM and HMM.
the proposed Action MACH method outperforms all other methods in the majority of experiments, including the recent approaches of [2, 4, 6, 7].
the Action MACH filter is a powerful and robust tool for action recognition in videos.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we introduce the first template based approach for action recognition that is able to synthesize a single filter for a given class of actions and is computationally efficient.
we introduce the Action MACH filter and show that this approach can be used to successfully recognize human actions from video sequences.

our approach is capable of recognizing actions from a wide range of datasets with a high degree of accuracy, and is able to recognize actions from videos with a high degree (over 90%) of background clutter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
our method is able to recognize a large variety of actions with a single template.
a template based approach is competitive with the state of the art in the field, and can provide an alternative solution for action recognition in the presence of occlusion and background clutter.
a single Action MACHI filter can be used for recognizing a given action class in a video.
